notes:
The District's recurring levy on an LLC is the Unincorporated Business Franchise Tax (Form D-30), and this record draws the Tennessee line through the middle of it. The tax is imposed for the privilege of carrying on a trade or business in the District, but its measure is the entity's taxable income at 8.25% - and the inclusion test excludes tax on income. What passes the substance test is the tax's floor: a $250 minimum, stepped to $1,000 when District gross receipts exceed $1 million, payable regardless of income once the business is over the filing threshold. The record therefore carries the floor - minimumAnnualUsd 250, basis revenue for the receipts-stepped minimum - and the income-measured component stays visible here: 8.25% of taxable income after a 30% salary allowance for owners and a $5,000 exemption, levied on the entity, not passed through. A reader who takes this record's franchise figures as the whole of DC's entity tax would be wrong in a loss year only; in a profitable year the 8.25% governs. This is the second entity-level income tax the namespace has met (Tennessee's excise was the first), the case its open thread said to watch for.
Two boundaries matter for who owes it at all. A business is exempt if more than 80% of gross income is from personal services rendered by the members and capital is not a material income-producing factor - a large class of professional LLCs is outside the tax entirely, and their income passes straight through to members. And only unincorporated businesses with gross receipts over $12,000 report at all, so a near-dormant LLC below that owes nothing; minimumAnnualUsd carries the floor an ordinary operating LLC pays, with the sub-$12,000 case here rather than as a Texas-style published 0, because the agency states $250 as the minimum tax rather than 0 as a no-tax-due tier.
firstYearExemption is false and is the record's weakest value: no page or provision read grants a first-year waiver, but no passage says an ordinary new LLC has none.
collectedWithAnnualReport is false, with a wrinkle specific to this jurisdiction: root states.json carries no DC record at all (50 states by design), so there is no annual_report_fee for this figure to be counted in. The District's report is the biennial report at the Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, carried by the entitysearch namespace; the franchise tax is a different payment to a different agency.
stateIncomeTax: the District taxes individuals at graduated rates topping at 10.75% above $1,000,000, so pass-through income of a UBFT-exempt LLC is taxed to its members. Where the entity itself paid the franchise tax, § 47-1803.02(a)(2)(D) excludes the member's distributive share from individual gross income to the extent it was already taxed against the business - the anti-double-taxation rule quoted in evidence. hasPTETElection is null, not false: no page read enumerates the District's elections, and the question is structurally different here because the UBFT already taxes the entity and the exclusion already does what a PTET's credit mechanism does elsewhere.
needsReview: Three loose ends. (1) hasPTETElection is null: no OTR page found that would name a pass-through entity tax election or its absence; the D-40 or D-65 instructions would settle it. (2) firstYearExemption false rests on the absence of any waiver on the pages and provisions read, not on a passage. (3) The definition of unincorporated business (§ 47-1808.01), which determines whether a particular LLC is in or out, was not quoted; the OTR rates page's exemption sentence carries the operative boundary.
